title: Why Are International Hotels Adopting DialZero Faster Than the U.S.? (Yes, We're Looking at You, America.)
author: Jonathan Bush
excerpt: One NYC hotel saved $40,000. International hotels are moving faster than the U.S. Here’s what you’re missing.
body:
The Wake-Up Call (Without the Hold Music)

Let’s be honest. Hotel guests today aren’t waking up hoping to call an operator. They're waking up wondering why they're still listening to hold music in 2025. Meanwhile, your front desk is juggling phones like it’s still 1998.

DialZero was built to fix that—and hotels around the world are catching on fast.

The Bold Move in New York

Let’s start at home. A bold hotel in New York removed landline phones from guest rooms completely. No, not a little test run. Gone. The result?

They’re now saving $40,000 a year.

That’s not a typo. That’s tens of thousands saved annually just by switching to DialZero’s QR-code-based guest communication. Guests scan. Guests chat. Staff responds instantly—without the telecom overhead.

Meanwhile, Abroad...

Hotels internationally are already ahead of the curve.
From boutique hotels in Lisbon to business resorts in India, they’re choosing DialZero to modernize their guest experience and reduce costs.

One chain in Europe is seeing a 32% reduction in guest service response times —all since implementing DialZero three months ago.

Another partner in Asia has cut guest-related call costs by over half and now includes our QR system in their digital concierge program.

So, yes—the rest of the world is doing the thing.

But Why the Delay in the U.S.?

Maybe it’s tradition. Maybe it’s fear of change. Maybe your current system feels “good enough.”

But here’s a little math:
If one New York hotel can save $40K per year with DialZero, how much are you losing by staying put?

And for the skeptics out there—yes, DialZero works with your PMS. Yes, it’s customizable. And no, your guests won’t have to download anything. It's just fast, personal service… without the headache.

Your Guests Expect Instant.

Let’s be real: guests can book flights, order food, and check into flights with a tap.
They shouldn’t be calling a front desk, waiting, repeating themselves, or getting transferred to another line like it’s a game of guest services telephone.

If your staff is burnt out and your guests are burnt up—there’s a solution.

Time to Join the Club

The international hotels are already on the wave. Your New York peers are saving thousands. And your guests? They’re already expecting something better.
